note: HUMAN-EDITABLE. This file is the single source of truth for the ranking. Each Monday, an AI proposes new scores (see scripts/weekly_rank.py + data/criteria.json); a human reviews, edits pros/cons, and commits. Every change is snapshotted to data/history/YYYY-MM-DD.json.
method: Weekly AI scoring against data/criteria.json, then human review. Scores are 0-10 per dimension; total is the weighted sum (0-100).

rankings.best_for: Self-hosted teams that want full control and zero license fees
cons: You operate it: Postgres + Redis for full spend tracking, plus upgrades and paging.
Python stack may add friction for Node.js-only shops.
Enterprise SSO and extras need a commercial license.
rankings.name: LiteLLM
pros: Unified OpenAI-compatible API across 100+ providers.
Virtual keys, per-team budgets, spend tracking, fallbacks, caching, guardrails.
Largest open-source community (58k+ stars); AWS multi-provider guidance is built on it.
rankings.tagline: The open-source standard: one API for 100+ providers, free to run.
rankings.token_saving: Self-hosted routing + caching with no platform fee; every dollar saved stays saved. Biggest lever for teams with steady traffic.

rankings.best_for: Teams that must pass a security review before shipping AI
cons: Now part of Palo Alto Prisma AIRS: evaluate platform direction, not the old startup.
Starts at $49/mo; serious governance tiers are custom-priced.
Semantic caching lives in hosted/enterprise editions.
rankings.name: Portkey
pros: 1,600+ models with guardrails, RBAC, audit logs, prompt management, MCP gateway.
SOC 2 / HIPAA / GDPR posture with signed DPAs.
Open-source gateway core (MIT) plus managed cloud path.
rankings.tagline: Governance-first gateway, now inside Palo Alto Networks.
rankings.token_saving: Budgets, cost-based limits and semantic caching enforce savings as policy, not hope.

rankings.best_for: Prototyping and evaluating hundreds of models with one key
cons: 5.5% fee on credit top-ups compounds at scale ($550/mo on $10k spend).
No semantic caching or prompt management; observability is activity logs only.
No self-host option; traffic passes through a third party.
rankings.name: OpenRouter
rankings.pricing: Pass-through model prices + 5.5% credit fee; free models available
pros: Widest managed catalog (300-500+ models) behind one endpoint.
Zero setup: change base URL and call any model; per-response usage.cost.
Free tier models for evaluation; BYOK escape hatch.
rankings.tagline: One key, hundreds of models. The fastest way to compare.
rankings.token_saving: Free models for eval; automatic provider failover avoids paid retries. Watch the top-up fee at production volume.

rankings.best_for: Enterprises already running Kong for API management
cons: Key AI plugins (semantic cache, advanced limits, MCP proxy) need Enterprise license.
Heavy if AI routing is the only reason to adopt Kong.
Entry pricing from ~$500/mo per control plane.
rankings.name: Kong AI Gateway
rankings.pricing: OSS core; Konnect managed; enterprise quote
pros: AI controls inside an already-audited API control plane.
Semantic cache, cost/token limits, PII guards, MCP + agent-to-agent governance.
Self-hosted or managed Konnect.
rankings.tagline: AI traffic governed where your APIs already live.
rankings.token_saving: Cost-based rate limiting plus semantic cache caps spend per consumer and model.

rankings.best_for: Teams already on Cloudflare Workers who want caching for free
cons: No provider failover or budget enforcement: errors reach your app.
Smaller model catalog; prompts pass through Cloudflare infra.
Cost analytics are dashboard-only, not per-request metadata.
rankings.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
pros: Zero-infra edge gateway: change base URL, get logs + caching.
Mature identical-request and semantic caching at the edge.
No token markup; tight Workers/R2 integration.
rankings.tagline: Free edge caching and observability for Cloudflare stacks.
rankings.token_saving: Edge caching is the cheapest saving there is: a cache hit costs nothing and adds no infra.

rankings.best_for: High-RPS services where tail latency is the constraint
cons: Narrower provider list than the big catalogs.
Self-hosted: you own uptime and upgrades.
Fewer governance extras out of the box.
rankings.name: Bifrost
pros: Go runtime with microsecond-level overhead; built for sustained throughput.
Drop-in OpenAI compatibility; no platform fees.
Small footprint next to Python-based proxies.
rankings.tagline: Raw speed: a Go gateway for high-volume inference.
rankings.token_saving: No fees plus fewer timeouts means fewer paid retries at scale.

rankings.best_for: Next.js apps deployed on Vercel using the AI SDK
cons: Convenience layer, not a control plane; off-Vercel it is awkward.
Budgets are soft caps and cover Vercel-billed spend only.
Platform concentration: hosting, framework and model access in one vendor.
rankings.name: Vercel AI Gateway
pros: Native to the AI SDK; OpenAI + Anthropic SDK compatibility.
No markup, consolidated billing on an invoice you already pay.
Automatic fallback across providers with full routing-attempt logs.
rankings.tagline: One endpoint for 100+ models, native to Vercel.
rankings.token_saving: Pass-through pricing with zero fee; per-team budgets catch runaway keys early.

rankings.best_for: Enterprises buying gateway + serving + evals as one platform
cons: Platform buy-in: heavier than a standalone gateway.
Entry pricing opaque beyond the starter tier.
Overkill if you only need routing.
rankings.name: TrueFoundry
pros: 1,000+ models with latency-based routing, quotas, guardrails, MCP gateway.
SaaS, VPC, on-prem and air-gapped deployment.
Request-level observability tied to evals.
rankings.tagline: Gateway plus serving plus evals, including air-gapped.
rankings.token_saving: Token quotas plus latency routing keep spend inside policy on every workload.

rankings.best_for: Teams that need to see exactly where every token went
cons: BYOK only: it observes spend, it does not cut model prices.
Thin on routing/fallback vs full gateways; more logging proxy than router.
Cloud plans from $79/mo; teams tier higher.
rankings.name: Helicone
pros: One-line integration with best-in-class per-request cost/latency logging.
Open-source core; cross-provider caching; health-aware fallback.
First step of every saving program: attribution before optimization.
rankings.tagline: Observability first: one line to see all your token spend.
rankings.token_saving: Finds the waste (Wednesday's 3x spike, the unused tool schema) so routing and caching have something to aim at.

rankings.best_for: EU teams wanting a wide catalog with per-token pricing
cons: 5% markup over provider prices; fee structure needs reading at volume.
No completed SOC 2 evidenced publicly; request the current report.
Smaller community than OpenRouter.
rankings.name: Requesty
pros: 700+ models with automatic cheapest-route selection.
EU data residency options; one key like OpenRouter.
BYOK escape hatch for production volume.
rankings.tagline: Wide catalog with automatic cheapest-route selection.
rankings.token_saving: Auto-routing to the cheapest provider for the same model is a direct per-token cut.
